title: Tenant-priority crediting rolling upgrade controller for capacity-safe dedicated pools
creator: Anjali Kapoor
description: Problem: During LTS and minor runtime upgrades for Dedicated GPU pools we frequently see short-lived capacity surges and SLA blips as tenants are evicted in waves. Current drain strategies are either naive (all-at-once) or purely time-windowed which fails to account for multi-tenant load variance and autoscaler reaction. This ticket introduces a new "priority crediting" controller and a deterministic autoscaler handshake protocol to enable tenant-aware, capacity-safe rolling upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller can compute and assign evacuation credits per tenant accounting for historical QPS and active in-flight token usage. 2) Upgrade waves proceed without causing >5% request error spike and maintain latency SLO for top-90th percentile across tenants. 3) Autoscaler handshake API is consumed by the cluster-autoscaler to reserve short-term headroom before eviction starts. 4) Full e2e simulation with synthetic tenants shows no more than 10% capacity variance beyond planned buffer across 100 simulated upgrades. 5) Rollback fastpath triggers automatically on observed token-loss or eviction-failure and brings pool to steady-state within 3 minutes.
design_summary: We propose a 3-part system: (A) Priority Crediter - a controller that tracks per-tenant credit balances derived from recent throughput, SLA tier, and active reservations. Credits throttle how many slots a tenant may relinquish during a wave. (B) Evacuation Negotiator - a bidirectional handshake with the autoscaler where the negotiator requests "reservation windows" (N GPUs for M minutes) and only starts soft-drain after reservation is confirmed. (C) Momentum & Safety Guards - conservative heuristics (evacuation momentum metric, drain opacity score, and slot-preservation tokens) to avoid cascading autoscaler scale-downs. The controller is pluggable into the existing upgrade orchestrator and exposes observation metrics and rollout gates for Console rollouts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement Priority Crediter and simple reservation API (2 weeks). Phase 2: Integrate with dummy autoscaler adapter and run cluster-level chaos sims (2 weeks). Phase 3: Wire into orchestrator, add rollout gate hooks and canary cohort logic (2 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual customer-facing rollout on non-critical Dedicated pools and monitor for two full upgrade cycles (2 weeks).
tradeoffs: - Stronger weighting for SLA tier reduces eviction fairness but protects key customers. - Reservation windows increase short-term cost (extra buffer) but drastically reduce service disruption risk. - More conservative credit decay reduces speed of upgrades for very active tenants; we may tune decay based on telemetry.
observability: Expose Prometheus metrics: tenant_credit_balance, negotiated_reserved_gpus, evacuation_momentum, drain_opacity_score, slot_preservation_tokens, upgrade_wave_progress. Add Console dashboard tile 'Rolling Upgrade Safety' with per-tenant credit heatmap and worst-case SLO delta. Emit structured events for each handshake and fastpath rollback. Ship synthetic canary telemetry during rollout for auto-alerting.
test_plan: Unit tests for credit arithmetic and reservation state machine. Integration test against a simulator that replays historical tenant traces (QPS, seq length distribution). Chaos test: random node terminations and network partitions while an upgrade wave is active. Performance test: ensure controller scales to 5000 tenants/region with sub-second credit recalculation cadence. Runbook test: step through rollback fastpath in staging and validate SLA restoration time.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to control-plane in staging. 2) Canary: enable on single non-critical pool with low-util tenants for one week. 3) Expand to 10% of Dedicated pools while maintaining automatic rollback gate. 4) Global enable after 4 successful waves and metrics stability. All rollouts guarded by rollout gates in Console and require manual approval for high-SLA pools.
rollback_plan: Immediate fastpath: cancel active reservations, re-inject preserved slot tokens to tenants, and mark pool as 'safety-hold' to stop new upgrades. Notify on-call and trigger automated rehydration of pods onto alternate compatible pools if available. Post-mortem runbook linked below.
